text:
sara: :rotating_light: seeing a weird auth pattern — multiple admin-role SAML assertions from same account but different user agents + very short gaps across regions. some sessions auto-revoked by our policy. anyone else?
chen: can you paste the auth event ids? also does this correlate with any recent RBAC changes?
sara: pasted snippet below
```
EventID: ev-20240415-9a1b
user: svc-jane
role: admin
ua: curl/7.79.1 (x86_64)
ip: 18.215.4.22 -> 3.231.12.9 (rapid switch)
action: assertion_grant
anomaly_score: 0.92
trigger: mfa_push_skipped?
```

david: wow that UA rotation + rapid geo jumps looks like credential stuffing + proxy chain. could be session token theft + reuse. did KMS rotate keys yesterday? KMS logs would show if any signing keys were reissued.
mira: checking KMS audit now. give me a minute. also checking our SSO provider's assertion logs.
security-bot: Automated alert: 2024-04-15 08:12Z - 23 similar assertion events flagged for user svc-jane, triggered "improbable-auth-chain" rule. Suggested action: revoke active sessions, block recent IPs for 1h.
chen: agree with revoke. can we quickly revoke all tokens for svc-jane and force a passwordless rebind? also create a temporary RBAC block for service accounts in the admin role until we have more context.
sara: revoking sessions now. command run: `authctl revoke-sessions --user svc-jane --all` :white_check_mark:

mira: KMS audit: no key rotation events in last 48h. there is one anomalous signer call from a worker pool IP that matches an unusual 3rd-party CI IP at 07:59Z. logging full call detail and forwarding to infra-sre.
david: if KMS didn't rotate, maybe attacker exfiltrated service account credentials. check who issued the service account creds and any recent RBAC grants around that service account. were there any policy changes to allow long-lived tokens?
chen: checked infra-iam: a policy change on 2024-04-14 allowed `iam.serviceAccounts.createToken` for the infra-automation role, approved in last-week rollout. I'm paginating the audit for which principal called that.
sara: notable: two lockouts happened for human user jthomas before these events. might be related (account takeover attempt then use of service key).
mira: forwarded KMS signer trace + SSO assertion chain to security ops channel, flagged for forensics.
security-bot: Action logged: sessions revoked for svc-jane, IPs 18.215.4.22 and 3.231.12.9 blocked in WAF for 1h, SSO provider rate-limited assertions for that tenant.
chen: next steps: 1) rotate service account keys for svc-jane, 2) audit any recent RBAC grants that modify token issuance, 3) enable stronger assertion validation (UA/Device fingerprinting), 4) add detection for short-interval multi-region assertion sequences.
david: agree. also add permanent SSO audit retention to 90d for tenant-level logs and enable KMS HSM access logging at higher verbosity. open a ticket for post-incident review and policy updates.
sara: created tracking issue: https://ourtracker/SEC-4219 - contains timeline, actions, and owners. tagging @mira @chen for follow-ups.
mira: will spearhead KMS forensics and sync with infra-sre. planning 1hr deep-dive in 30m.
chen: I'll scrub RBAC diffs and push rollback for the infra-automation change if we see it's root cause.
david: communications: customer-facing teams — none impacted as this is internal service account; but recommend security advisory note for internal SREs. I'll draft short comms.
sara: postmortem owners: mira (forensics), chen (RBAC/root cause), david (comm), sara (remediation tracking).
security-bot: Post-incident checklist created: SEC-4219, status: containment done, investigation in progress.
mira: initial ETA for full forensics report 48-72h. will include KMS signer traces, SSO assertion chains, and recommended controls (shorter token TTLs, enrollment of service accounts into device-fingerprint checks).
chen: quick wins added to the ticket: disable long-lived token grants for non-human principals, add alert on >3 assertions for same principal within 2m coming from >2 regions, require service accounts to use key rotation every 24h where possible.
sara: thanks team. keep thread updated and ping me in #sec-oncall for urgent notes. :thumbsup:
